qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md (line 21: gates must exclude convincing dead apps via independent-context readback)
.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/task/tests/scoring.toml, tests/tools/score.py (identical to template), tests/test.sh lines 203-224, tests/app_context.md
evidence: Real gates: scoring.toml [gates] render=0.0, constraints=0.0; score.py (byte-identical to template) requires each gate score > 0.0 and zeroes reward otherwise; test.sh 213-224 runs the gates suite first and exits before scored on failure. Both gate judge.toml use aggregation=all_pass with one binary criterion. Render gate (authenticated_render): fresh browser, real Kittle & Rowe matter chat not blank/static mock/generic error/fatal error, nothing private before sign-in, wrong password rejected, gwen@kittle.test opens her matters and messages. Constraints gate (server_backed_local_application): gwen posts 'Gate check JUDGE-G1' in M-11, reload shows it, and a SEPARATE browser context signed in as harriet sees it -> excludes a localStorage/first-paint facade, satisfying REVIEW_POLICY line 21. In-dimension gate: functional, polish and visual prompt.md each carry 'Global browser gate: ... loads from http://localhost:3000 without a fatal browser error ... gwen@kittle.test can sign in and see protected content ... A blank page, empty workspace, static mock, static shell, missing backend, or seeded-looking facade fails this gate. Protected content must contain real task data backed by the running local server ... If the gate fails, assign 0 to every criterion in this dimension.' This restates the template gate and strengthens it with static-shell and backing legs; polish/visual also state 'The global browser gate is the only all-or-nothing rule'. No partial credit on gate failure. Same-origin: task.toml network_mode='public'; every gate and scored prompt explicitly says 'External font, script, or CDN asset requests are allowed', the constraints criterion says 'Under the declared public network posture, external font, script, or CDN asset requests are allowed and must not fail this gate'; grep for origin finds only functional prompt line 40 ('replays are in-page calls from the app's origin'), which is a replay mechanism, not a gate condition. 'loads from http://localhost:3000' is the app URL the instruction requires, not an asset-origin restriction. The older Internal Quality Checks wording ('cross-origin apps') is superseded by the Quality Checks row and the public-network notes. Individual-mode functional: each per-criterion session receives the same prompt with the gate, so a failing gate zeroes every functional criterion across sessions. Counterexample probing: (a) broken app that could pass - a client-side static shell with seeded JSON and client-side password check could pass render and the scored-prompt gate's visual impression, but fails the constraints gate because harriet's separate context cannot see JUDGE-G1; a server that accepts posts but serves no sign-in fails render. (b) conforming app that could fail - an app loading Google Fonts/CDN scripts is explicitly allowed; an app that shows matters first and messages after selecting one still satisfies 'opens her matters and their messages'; after functional writes gwen keeps M-11/M-13 (walls only target staff and are lifted; persistence criterion restores Sian's wall/timer), so polish/visual gate does not see an empty workspace. Runtime: the frozen-hash scripted golden (functional.cjs 99-106, functional-before.json 'gate_constraints': true; server.js hash 03b5...ddadd matches frozen) followed the constraints gate steps; render gate and configured-judge gate runs are not measured, which is outside this structural row but not claimed here.
run_verdict: PASS (source/structure; constraints-gate steps observed in scripted golden, not a configured judge run)
